inputs.original_text: The IOC’s “fairness and safety” line is a carefully packaged justification for deciding who counts and who gets shut out. The ban on transgender women and DSD athletes in the female category at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and future Games lets the institution set the boundary, then disguise that choice as neutral science. Coventry’s claim — “It would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category” — makes the policy sound inevitable and discourages scrutiny. The real issue is who controls the rules and the story told about them.
inputs.modified_text: This is bigger than a “fairness” debate. The IOC gets to draw the line around who counts, then presents its own decision as neutral science—as if Coventry’s claim, “It would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category,” settles the matter rather than shutting down scrutiny. The ban on transgender women and DSD athletes in the female category at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and future Games looks like a way to consolidate control over the rules while directing public anger at the people being excluded. The real question is who benefits when the institution gets to define the categories and control the story.
